text: A Client Script runs in the user's browser, not on ServiceNow's server. That's a very different world from the Business Rules and Script Includes you spent Chapter 3 writing, and it changes what is actually reachable from inside your code, and what isn't, in ways that trip up a lot of developers coming from server-side work.

In the browser, a Client Script has access to g_form, the form the user is currently looking at, and g_user, information about the logged-in session. What it does not have is GlideRecord - that's a server-side class with no implementation in browser-side JavaScript at all. The server is the only place with full database access.

If you try to create a GlideRecord inside a Client Script, it simply does not exist - you'll get an error, not a result. This isn't a bug to work around; it's a deliberate security boundary. The browser is code running on a machine ServiceNow doesn't control, in a session a user could inspect or rewrite with their own browser's developer tools at any time.

GlideAjax is the bridge that lets a Client Script ask the server a specific, pre-approved question safely. From the browser, you create a new GlideAjax pointed at a specific Script Include, name the method you want to call with sysparm_name, and pass along any parameters it needs. Then you call getXMLAnswer with a callback function to receive the eventual result.

The round trip has four steps. Step one, the Client Script builds and names the call, entirely in the browser. Steps two and three, the request travels to the server, and the named Script Include method actually runs there, with full GlideRecord access the browser itself never gets. Step four, a callback function back in the browser receives whatever result the server sent back.

That callback does not run on the very next line of code after the GlideAjax call - it runs later, asynchronously, once the server actually responds, which can be a surprising gap for anyone used to synchronous server-side scripts. Keep that in mind; next lesson builds the Script Include side of this bridge, and the lesson after that wires up the client side in full, end to end.
